page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-16-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a single 402 GB local NVMe SSD, while no dedicated GPU hardware is included. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector extensions (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core execution and Geekbench text processing scoring in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and database operations fall within the average range. However, memory subsystem performance exhibits notable tradeoffs. While cached small-block read bandwidth is average, large-block uncached read bandwidth is weak, and large-block uncached write bandwidth is poor, landing in the bottom 10%. Similarly, while the instance handles small and medium LLM inference workloads with average efficiency, prompt processing performance for large 70B models is poor due to the lack of hardware accelerators and memory bandwidth constraints.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-standard-16-lssd offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring dedicated compute resources and fast local scratch space without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The integrated 402 GB NVMe SSD provides high-speed local storage directly bundled with the instance, making it highly suitable for database operations, web serving, text processing, and general-purpose application hosting. It is less suited for memory-bound large-scale data processing or large language model inference.
